quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Information technology project managers plan, initiate and manage IT projects, lead and guide technical staff, act as the link between the business and technical sides, and monitor progress against deadlines, standards and cost targets.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Information Technology Project Managers) include IT Program Manager, IT Project Manager, Cybersecurity Project Manager and Scrum Master.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What an IT program manager does
paragraphs: Information technology project managers plan, initiate and manage IT projects, lead and guide technical staff, act as the link between the business and technical sides, and monitor progress against deadlines, standards and cost targets.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Information Technology Project Managers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Manage project execution so that it stays within budget, schedule and scope.
Work with project staff to identify and resolve problems.
Initiate, review or approve changes to project plans.
